issue.body:
# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On likebus.ua the site pins two fixed app-promotion bars over the mobile page (an install bar at the top, which the reporter boxed, and an app-download bar at the bottom covering results); the rule likebus.ua#⁠#⁠#⁠likebus-app-banner, #⁠appStickyBottom hides both and was verified in the filtered browser with the page left intact. I placed it in the Mobile App Banners filter, which is where this repository keeps app-install banner rules. ## Rule `likebus.ua###likebus-app-banner, #appStickyBottom` ## Policy rationale Not the site's own paid advertising or a paywall:⁠ the target is the site's app-install/app-download promotion, which the AdGuard Mobile App Banners annoyance filter exists to remove and which the reporter filed as an Annoyance. Not an anti-adblock wall, scam or phishing page:⁠ the page loads normally with its content, and no detector script or gate is involved. The two fixed bars consume \~140px of an 812px mobile viewport and cover the site header and the first result cards, so the policy exception for unobtrusive non-animated header banners does not apply. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The events page at restaurantcounter.co.uk shows a self-hosted CookieConsent ("We use cookies!") card fixed over the page plus its floating cookie-settings button. The verified rule restaurantcounter.co.uk#⁠#⁠#⁠cc--main, #⁠cookie-settings hides both, leaves the page intact, and belongs with the existing cookie-notice rules in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt. ## Rule `restaurantcounter.co.uk###cc--main, #cookie-settings` ## Policy rationale The report is a first-party cookie-consent notice overlapping page content; none of the run instruction's closing rules apply (not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, not a scam/phishing page). It is not an anti-adblock wall at all, so no detector-script gate applies. Element hiding is the least invasive fix and matches the maintainer guidance to hide the notice when that is enough; it is also a basic CSS-selector rule, so it works in the reporter's Safari content-blocker model as well as the browser extension and desktop apps. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41766717517 Automated analysis against filters at `f2c955f`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — bus.tickets.ua shows a full-width app-install promo bar ("Travel easier with our app" + "Use app" Play Store button + close X) at the very top of every page, directly above the site header; the reporter circled exactly that bar. Hiding it with bus.tickets.ua#⁠#⁠.app-top-banner was verified in the AdGuard CLI baseline (bar visible, then hidden with no leftover gap, page intact) and is filed in the Mobile App Banners filter. ## Rule `bus.tickets.ua##.app-top-banner` ## Policy rationale The report is a mobile-app-install banner annoyance, the category the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter is defined to block; none of the run instruction's close rules (site's own third-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock wall, anti-adblock without a captured detector script, scam/phishing page) applies. The Mobile App Banners policy limitation on non-animated header/menu banners was weighed:⁠ the element is a full-width standalone promo strip with its own CTA and close control placed above, not inside, the site's header element, so it is treated as blockable; the judgment is recorded for the reviewing maintainer. No existing filter expression covers the element (no rule for .app-top-banner or #⁠app-top-banner; the shared #⁠#⁠.app-banner family uses a different class), so a new cosmetic rule is required rather than an extension. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/f2c955ffc54a331e71160a8315d6715c533b6419/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On tokubai.co.jp a full-screen first-party campaign/app-download popup (div.popup_banner_image) covers the leaflet page while a web2app cover clips the leaflet gallery and locks body scroll. A domain-scoped trusted-click-element scriptlet that dismisses the popup and the 'このままウェブで見る' app-gate was verified in the CLI proxy:⁠ popup gone, leaflet fully rendered and scroll restored, page integrity intact. ## Rule `tokubai.co.jp#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.popup_banner_image .close_button.close_popup, .cover_web2app__read_more_on_web', '', '1000')` ## Policy rationale The reported overlay is the site's own campaign/app-download promo gated over the leaflet content, handled under the annoyance filters' stated purposes (Popups:⁠ popups that introduce the site's features; Mobile App Banners:⁠ banners that promote the site's mobile app), not first-party ad inventory, so the 'first-party advertising' carve-out does not close it. Element hiding was tried first (tokubai.co.jp#⁠#⁠.popup_banner_image) and was not enough because the app-install cover and the clipped leaflet survived; a scriptlet that dismisses the gate is the justified next step under the maintainer rule 'hide the popup when that is enough'. No policy rule blocks rule generation for this annoyance report, and the rule is domain-scoped to tokubai.co.jp. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/95db9bb4cd80f84d92692158b30448ff9cf9707b/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |
## Artifacts https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/41770217989 Automated analysis against filters at `95db9bb`. Posted by a filters agent; a maintainer reviews before anything is merged.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking) [https://chat.mozilla.org/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchat.mozilla.org%2F) ### Comment > The AdGuard CookieNotices filterlist contains a cosmetic filter that interferes with the Element Web client for Matrix. I an demosnstrating this on the web client hosted at chat.mozilla.org, but likely other instances of this popular web client are also affected. > > When you log in to your Matrix account from a new device, you are strongly advised to verify the new login from another device where you were already logged in. This verification is requried for encrypted messages to become readable, among other purposes. > The interfering filtering rule (`.mx_ToastContainer`) ends up hiding the popup where the user is supposed to accept or decline the verification request. The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Not reproduced — The reported Bing search ad cannot be reproduced:⁠ the unfiltered control and the reporter's own filter configuration both load the reported query with only organic results (no ad container, no ad label, no ad request in the HAR), and complete full-page vision of the current extension session reports the symptom absent. Recommending closure as not reproduced; the reporter's unverified "Silver Fox trojan" claim about the linked domain, which now ranks organically, is left for a maintainer.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Policy rationale

No rule of the run instruction's filter policy closes this report:⁠ the reported problem is not a paywall, not a German or other anti-adblock wall, and not a first-party ad of a content site (the only candidate location, the advertiser's own destination, is a third-party site), so rule generation was allowed for this run. The reported defect could not be produced:⁠ no ad instance, ad label or ad placeholder appears on the loaded reported page in either environment, so there is no rule to write for it.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"5f76589bc6d86a35b1c1f0eb4095d6eb98b287dd569013649364f72fb7ef542f"} -->
The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — In two live sessions of onlineradiobox.com (desktop en-US and mobile ja-JP, complete full-page vision) through the AdGuard CLI baseline the reported anti-adblock modal never appears:⁠ the page loads fully, no such dialog exists in the DOM or the page text, and no Ad-Shield/html-load detector request is made, while AdGuard Base already injects the Ad-Shield countermeasure scriptlets for this domain. The report could not be reproduced and no new rule has evidence behind it, so it is recommended for closing.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's closing rules do not apply to this report:⁠ it is not the site's own advertising, not a paywall, and the wall in the reporter's screenshot is a Japanese-language anti-adblock modal on a US-domain site, so the 'German anti-adblock wall' close rule does not cover it. Because no repository rule closes this report, the run recorded allow_rule_generation; rule generation was open, but no rule could be derived or validated because the reported defect was absent in every environment this run could execute. The instruction's anti-adblock gate ('write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer') was also unmet:⁠ the captured request inventory of both loaded sessions contains no html-load.com / Ad-Shield detector request at all, so no new anti-adblock rule has evidence behind it.

## Missing information

- No way to load the reporter's settings import in the adguard_cli route: Issue #⁠246218 carries a reporter settings import URL (AdGuard for Android profile with Fanboy's Annoyances and two custom subscriptions). The locked adguard_cli environment declares those third-party sources as skippedSources, and `launch_browser` refuses `settings` for an `extension:"none"` session ("A control session (extension \⁠"none\⁠") runs no blocker and takes no \⁠"settings\⁠""), offering only an `extension:"prepared"` blocker instead. The run instruction gives no way to form a `reported_on_current` reporter-parity session in the CLI route, so the reporter's exact configuration cannot be compared with the CLI baseline and the controlled reporter-vs-defaults comparison the instruction asks for cannot be run.

## Artifacts

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter-circled defect on nwknews.jp is a sponsored Amazon "Fire TV Stick 4K Select" product card (rel="nofollow sponsored" Amazon links, product image from m.media-amazon.com) injected inside the article body; no baseline rule hides it. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule was verified in the AdGuard CLI proxy:⁠ the card was visible before and gone after, with no remaining instances, no page damage and no ad-layout residue. ## Rule `nwknews.jp##div[class^="article-body"] table[style*="border:1px solid #ddd"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's closing rules cover first-party self-promotion, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls and anti-adblock walls without a captured detector script; this report is none of those. The reported element is a sponsored affiliate product card (rel="nofollow sponsored", Amazon Associates tag omosironetton-22) inserted into the article body, not the site's editorial content or its own products, and the Japanese filter already blocks the same class of Amazon affiliate unit on nwknews.jp. The symptom is reproduced on the filtered baseline and the candidate rule was verified by the environment experiment with an intact page. ## Place in the list [JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2ce65f5aeeb216e53e01efdea5828ffdfd535789/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 846](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/2ce65f5aeeb216e53e01efdea5828ffdfd535789/JapaneseFilter/sections/specific.txt#L846). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported Netflix watch page is unreachable in this run:⁠ /watch/81011359 302-redirects to the non-member title page for 뤼팽 both in the reporter-settings proxy session and in an extension-less CLI-route session, and no Netflix session is available, so the circled playback area was never observable (full-page vision confirms the marketing/title page, not the watch page). The only rule decisions on that page were tracker blocks (||netflix.com/log/, ||netflix.com/api/ftl/probe?monotonic=, ||onetrust.com^$third-party), and since the report names no broken element, no evidence-backed rule can be proposed or validated.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's annotated region on fonbet.by/sports is the full-width cookie-consent bar fixed at the bottom of the page, and the baseline filters leave it visible; the rule `fonbet.by##div[class^="cookie-alert"]` hides it (merging into the repository's existing shared selector) with no layout damage. Verified in the A/B/C experiment:⁠ selector visible on the baseline page, hidden with the candidate, page integrity intact. ## Rule `fonbet.by##div[class^="cookie-alert"]` ## Policy rationale The run instruction's filter policy closes only first-party advertising, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, and anti-adblock reports without a captured detector script; the reporter-defined target here is a cookie-consent notice, not any of those, and no anti-adblock wall, paywall or third-party ad appears on the page. The AdGuard Cookie Notices filter exists to block cookie notices and CMP requests, and the maintainer rules allow a cosmetic hide when the page then works — the verified after-state shows the page fully functional with the bar removed. The repository already carries the identical selector for gameplay.pl, so the fix belongs to that shared rule family and the host merges the fonbet.by-scoped candidate into it. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/9203aed27915efeb09b00a9c6c447dc0f2da9de5/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
